payload.rebuttal: fixed: Confirmed by reading session.py: run_one_cell creates run_id/task_id before opening the try block whose only handler (BaseException at session.py:1765-1775) re-raises the original exception untouched, so a crash after real attempts have already billed real cost_usd_est reaches run_batch's except clause with no run_id at all — my comment's claim that nothing was charged was false, and the real bug was that attach_run_to_batch was never called for that run, leaving its batch_id NULL forever and silently excluding real spend from ledger.batch_spend's budget-gate join. Since saffron/cell/session.py is forbidden, I fixed it from batch.py: record the high-water mark on runs.run_id immediately before each candidate's call, and on a raise, sweep in any run minted since then (run_id > high_water AND batch_id IS NULL) via ledger.attach_run_to_batch, rather than relying on the outcome object the raise never returns. Scoping by run_id > high_water rather than every batch_id IS NULL row is deliberate: a ledger accumulates plenty of those from saffron cell and replay.py, which pass no batch on purpose, and sweeping all of them would fold an unrelated past run's spend into tonight's batch; under K=1 nothing else can mint a run while one candidate's call is in flight, so this is exactly the set that call produced. Added tests/test_batch.py::test_a_crash_after_real_spend_still_counts_against_the_next_budget_gate, which reproduces the exact scenario (a runner that mints a real run/task/40-dollar attempt against a 50-dollar batch, then raises) and asserts the second, 20-dollar candidate is correctly refused by the budget gate and the crashed run's batch_id is stamped — this fails without the fix (remaining reads 50 instead of 10). All 10 required witnesses plus this new test pass; full suite, ruff and ty are clean.
